body:
Editor project/tag reads now overlap native modal rendering after the current resource is read. Only opening context reads opt into immediate transport; default cancellation and read bounds remain. The opening tag catalog is consumed once, with fresh invalidations and retries. Quiet seven-round release comparisons improve constrained editor opening by 65–82 ms across four workloads; a quiet repeat confirms 71–72 ms. Small local opening repeats at 74 to 31 ms. All 168 measured editor openings retain current source versions and both context reads.

The full gate passes 441 tests, all 25 Chromium suites, nine affected WebKit suites and broad HTTPS/planning checks. Regressions verify current versions, cancellation, reentrant ownership and rejection of an older tag response. A default eager-read prototype is rejected after a reproduced Calendar transition failure; the selected mode passes that unchanged scenario.

The existing manual app is rebuilt/restarted at the same HTTPS address, preserving 64 prior resource versions, two pins, preferences and certificate. All 33 served assets match the build; the owner card is unchanged. Evidence: progress/2026-10-01-editor-read-overlap.md. The broader performance objective and release acceptance remain open; desktop engine tests do not prove physical iPhone acceptance.

metadata.summary: Fresh editor reads overlap rendering with verified latency gains
